title: Dedicated burst-credit reconciliation failure due to scheduler clock drift
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Several Dedicated tenants experienced unexpected early burst exhaustion and soft-denial of burst requests during peak traffic windows. The behavior manifested as tenants hitting 'burst limit' and falling back to lower-capacity models or degraded latency despite having available reserved pool headroom. Customer-facing symptom: 5-30s cold starts for chat generation calls and 429-like throttles for burst allocations.

2026-03-09 09:12 UTC - First alert from observability: surge in tenant burst-deny events.
2026-03-09 09:24 UTC - Support ticket from AureliaCommerce reporting degraded SLA.
2026-03-09 10:00 UTC - Oncall routed to autoscaler and billing teams.
2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - Initial mitigation: increased soft headroom for affected pool.
2026-03-12 16:40 UTC - Deep-dive started; evidence of negative ledger adjustments correlated with scheduler clock offsets.

reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy a tenant to a Dedicated pool with burst credits.
2) Simulate a sustained 5-10 RPS burst for 30+ minutes.
3) Introduce a clock offset on the scheduler host (e.g., NTP stop -> +120 seconds drift).
4) Observe reconciliation loop that backfills/rolls-over credits using wall-clock timestamps instead of monotonic counters.
5) Verify burst ledger shows negative deltas and allocation controller denies new burst allocations despite pool headroom.
investigation_notes:
- Telemetry connected a spike in 'burst_denied' events to entries in the burst-credit-ledger where delta timestamps were non-monotonic.
- The allocator service uses timestamp-based reconciliation between 'scheduler' and 'billing' components. A scheduler clock skew allowed an older ledger entry to appear newer, causing double-application of a debit.
- Affected tenants spanned Hosted and Dedicated, but Private/on-prem tenants were disproportionately impacted when their NTP was misconfigured (air-gapped setups).
- Existing safeguards expected monotonic token counters; we used wall-clock to compute TTL and reconciliation windows in two places (allocator and biller) leading to race under skew.
- Post-deploy metrics show per-tenant burst balance stabilizes when reconciler switches to monotonic sequence numbers.
root_cause: Race in the burst-credit reconciliation path where wall-clock timestamps (non-monotonic under clock drift) were used to order ledger updates. When scheduler clock moved backward or large drift occurred, ledger entries were replayed and debits double-applied, artificially reducing tenant burst budgets and triggering allocations to be denied despite physical headroom.
workaround:
- For affected pools, temporarily enable 'allow-burst-if-reserved-headroom' to bypass ledger check (applied to 3 impacted regions).
- Advise Private tenants to ensure NTP is running and synchronized; provide a temporary cron to restart NTP in air-gapped manifests.
- Increased monitoring alert thresholds to detect abrupt negative deltas in burst-ledger.
fix_summary:
1) Rework reconciliation to use monotonic sequence IDs emitted by the scheduler rather than wall-clock timestamps.
2) Add idempotency guards to ledger application so replays do not double-apply debits.
3) Add a health check that surfaces clock-drift >5s on hosts participating in allocation protocol.
4) Add migration script to repair ledgers that show inconsistent sequence gaps.
rollback_plan: If the new reconciler causes regressions, revert to the previous code path and immediately enable 'allow-burst-if-reserved-headroom' for impacted pools while we hotfix. Reversion time target: <15 minutes. DB schema unchanged; ledger-app idempotency toggles via feature flag.
rollout_plan:
1) Canary deploy reconciler in us-west-2 for non-critical tenants (3% traffic).
2) Observe burst_denied and ledger-stability metrics for 24 hours.
3) Expand to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 incrementally (25% -> 60% -> 100%) with 2-hour evaluation gates.
4) After full rollouts, run repair migration during low-traffic window to fix any affected ledgers.
5) Communicate with enterprise customers one hour before migration.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests: ledger idempotency and monotonic ordering.
- Integration: simulated clock skew runner in our CI that injects +/- 120s drift and validates no double-debit.
- Load test: sustained burst traffic with random host clock offsets across 50 hosts for 2 hours.
- Acceptance criteria: no increase in 'burst_denied' vs baseline, median allocation latency unchanged.

notes: This ticket surfaced a subtle assumption about time ordering in a distributed ledger used for resource accounting. The fix is defensive and also improves correctness under common private deployment misconfigurations. Consider a broader audit of any subsystems that mix wall-clock with distributed reconciliation.
